fertilizer_research_notes: Values for phosphorus and potassium reflect P2O5 and K2O equivalent application rates. Because groundnut (Arachis hypogaea) is a legume capable of biological nitrogen fixation via Rhizobium, synthetic nitrogen requirements are low (starter nitrogen only, around 10–20 kg N/ha). Standard ISRA extension recommendations in the Bassin Arachidier typically call for approximately 150 kg/ha of NPK starter fertilizer formulation (e.g., 6-20-10 or 6-20-15) supplemented with gypsum/calcium application at pegging where soil calcium is deficient. Climate requirements and growth cycles reflect standard varieties cultivated in Senegal (e.g., short-cycle 90-day vs long-cycle 120-day varieties).

drought_tolerance.description: Groundnut exhibits moderate to high drought resistance during early vegetative stages, but remains highly sensitive to moisture stress during flowering, pegging, and early pod filling stages.

fertilizer_research_notes: Phosphorus and potassium are expressed as P2O5 and K2O. The CDH program contains no mineral 10-10-20 basal dose in the classic matrix but applies 200 kg/ha 10-10-20 at three crop stages, totaling 600 kg/ha and therefore 60 N, 60 P2O5 and 120 K2O kg/ha per cycle. citeturn30search14turn30search11 Senegal research has also tested a much lower microdose system on gombo in the Bassin Arachidier: 219 kg/ha 10-10-20 combined with 5-10 t/ha organic manure; this demonstrates that mineral-fertilizer application can be reduced under localized placement and organic nutrient supply, but it is not treated here as the standard full-field requirement. citeturn31search4 The min/max fields are a standardized minus/plus 20% screening envelope around the conventional CDH central rate. FAO EcoCrop gives okra unusually broad textural tolerance, including heavy, medium and light soils, provided drainage is adequate. citeturn23search2 Accordingly, gombo receives one of the broadest clay/sand envelopes in this dataset, while waterlogged Deck depressions remain unsuitable unless drained. fertilizer_research_notes: Salade is normalized here to lettuce, Lactuca sativa, which is the crop called laitue in CDH documentation. Phosphorus and potassium are P2O5 and K2O. The classic CDH recommendation is 250 kg/ha 10-10-20 at establishment followed by 250 and 400 kg/ha at approximately 20 and 40 days after planting, totaling 900 kg/ha 10-10-20 and therefore 90 N, 90 P2O5 and 180 K2O kg/ha. citeturn30search14turn30search11 The min/max values are a standardized minus/plus 20% engineering envelope around this central CDH application because the source does not publish separate minimum and maximum physiological requirements. Salade can be grown on sandy Niayes soils, but because it has a shallow root system and short intensive cycle, extremely low CEC makes nutrient and moisture control fragile; 5 cmol(+)/kg is therefore used as the lower filter and 8-18 cmol(+)/kg as the preferred range under commercial conditions. fertilizer_research_notes: Poivron is treated as sweet pepper, Capsicum annuum. Phosphorus and potassium are P2O5 and K2O. The CDH full-cycle program consists of about 500 kg/ha 10-10-20 as basal fertilizer plus 200 kg/ha at approximately 15, 30, 50 and 80 days after transplanting, a total of 1300 kg/ha and therefore 130 N, 130 P2O5 and 260 K2O kg/ha. citeturn30search14turn30search11 Contemporary Senegal horticulture teaching material reproduces the same 500 kg/ha basal plus four 200 kg/ha maintenance schedule. citeturn31search0 The min and max are a minus/plus 20% engineering envelope around this CDH center because the underlying technical sheet provides a prescription rather than formal minimum/maximum nutrient-response thresholds. The local description favors crumbly sandy-loamy, humus-rich and well-drained soil that is not excessively light. citeturn31search0 FAO EcoCrop for Capsicum annuum identifies medium/organic texture as optimal and medium/light texture within the broader tolerance, supporting Sandy Loam and Loam as the main USDA classes. citeturn26search1 The 8-30% clay and 40-80% sand range is therefore a quantitative recommendation-engine envelope rather than a literal ISRA granulometric limit. A minimum CEC of 5 and preferred range of 8-18 cmol(+)/kg are used to separate extremely weakly buffered sands from more reliable commercial pepper soils; productive Niayes soils have measured CEC around 8-34 cmol(+)/kg. citeturn28search6

drought_tolerance.description: FAO classifies pepper as having medium-high sensitivity to drought; FAO 56 also gives sweet pepper a low allowable depletion fraction (p≈0.30).
